title: Retire the FetchFailure re-export alias (OD-12, half 2 of 2)
body:
**Half two of two.** Follows the import move that landed as #180. Together they are the code half of **OD-12**, split so neither half is red on a required check. Recorded as **ESC-25** and its correction row.

`transcripts.py` re-exported `FetchFailure` in mypy's explicit `X as X` form, so the type was reachable through a module that does not define it.

OD-12 settled that. The type is the ledger's record, and the placement the shim papered over was circular in the direction that matters: **the ledger is what the transcript stage reports failures to.** Two blind authors agreed on the ledger's behaviour and disagreed on where its types live, and the orchestrator closed the gap by assigning modules ad hoc — which is the whole reason OD-12 exists.

#180 moved the only import that reached the type through this module, so removing the alias is inert. Nothing named it here any more.

The comment that used to defend the shim is already gone: R1013 (#179) replaced that block while rewriting the imports around it, and the module-placement reasoning it carried now sits with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT`, where OD-12 put it.

**Why the split.** `test-the-tests` reverts a pull request's implementation and requires the suite to go red. This change adds no behaviour: `transcripts.FetchFailure` still resolves at run time either way, and what goes is mypy's re-export marking, a TYPE-level constraint pytest cannot observe. So the whole change kept together can never satisfy that check. The owner chose the split over a red merge. `test-the-tests` skips this pull request because it touches no file under `tests/`, which is honest and is why the escape exists to record it.

Both commits carry `Split-Of: od-12-fetchfailure-shim`. No check reads that trailer — it is the third candidate ESC-25's correction row asks for, done by hand so this split is visible in the history rather than surviving only in the ledger.

**Plan.** `docs/plans/corpus-and-checkpoint.md`, whose OD-12 paragraph ratifies `FetchFailure`, `HaltTriggered` and `Ledger` in `ledger.py`.

**No blind tests, and none apply.** This removes an alias. It adds no behaviour and no test.

1255 passing, unchanged. `ruff check .` clean, `mypy src tests` clean over 42 files — and mypy is what enforces the rule going forward: under `--no-implicit-reexport`, any module importing `FetchFailure` from `transcripts` is now an error.
